tools.name: search_components
tools.description: Find the Echo UI item for a job ("a settings toggle", "confirm a delete") or by name. Leads with the best fit, or says plainly that Echo has nothing for the job yet, then lists every match with its install command. The cheapest way to find out what exists, and the first call before writing Echo code

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: The full record for one component: description, install command, usage (imports + smallest working snippet), composition (part tree), examples, accessibility, motion & sound, prop table and anti-patterns. tools.name: get_tokens
tools.description: The token families: Layer-3 semantic colour roles (--echo-*), sound names, motion's whole vocabulary — the motion tokens, the spring presets, the morph feels and the CSS duration and ease steps — and the shadow recipes. tools.name: get_examples
tools.description: Just the usage examples for one component, without the rest of its record. For when the component is already chosen and only its calling convention is needed.

tools.name: get_accessibility
tools.description: The accessibility rules a consumer of Echo can still get wrong — names on controls, form errors, announcements, focus and target size — and, with a name, what that component's accessibility was actually tested against. Echo guarantees WCAG 2.2 AA; this is the part the guarantee cannot cover for you.

tools.description: Echo's own styles, the looks Echo publishes, each with its one line and its fingerprint on the seven axes styles are placed on; or, with a name, one of them in full: its settings, rules, refusals, fonts, decisions and the slop police's word. tools.description: Whether a style.json is one Echo can apply, as `npx echo-ui-cli style check` says it: what stops it, the device it makes (light or dark), what the theme corrects for AA contrast, what the slop police stops (with the question for the builder) or the builder kept, and the decisions it leaves open.
